main_text.p: ctum stipulationi continenter adie-ctum, per omnes eius partes diffundi-tur, eamq; universam immutat. Itaque nostrum pactum non modò fortis, sed etiam usurarum debitionem divisit: ut iam nō totius fortis, quam totam hoc tempore non debeo, sed eius primæ pensionis, quam solam nunc debeo, usuræ commissæ sint. F. At pacta non pertinent ad usuras. debesi enim ex pacto usuræ pecunię creditę nō possunt. Itaque pactum nostrum (quod de sorte, sine ulla usurarum mentione, factũ est) ad eam partem stipulationis, in qua de usuris cautur, nō pertinet: nec eam immutauit, aut divisit. D. An pactum de sorte per partes soluenda, cō-tinenter adiectum ei stipulationi quæ de sorte & usuris facta est, nō ad utran-que stipulationis partē pertineat: sed ad eam duntaxat, in qua de sorte cautū est. controuersia non ex scripto & sententia, ut quidam putant, sed ex eorū contrarie scriptorum contentione nata est, quæ superius expositimus. Paulus hac de re consultus respondet, ad utranque partem pertinere. ac proin-de

page.notes: Running head (top right) is in heavy decorative type and could not be read; left as illegible. A small dot in the right margin beside "proin-" is a mark, not a note. Faint marks at the lower left are show-through and were left out. "debesi" in "debesi enim" is a doubtful reading and should be checked against the scan: the printed word appears to be "deberi" with the r partly obscured. "superius expositimus" appears as printed; the scan shows "exposuimus" and is likely a misprint for "exposuimus", kept as printed here. "pecunię" and "contrarie" are kept with their printed ę and è; the accents are hard to make out at this resolution. The paragraph continues onto the next page.
